https://www.wcpo.com/news/local-news/eas.text: Neighbors say they’ve complained for years about the property where a child was shot on Tuesday night in East Price Hill.East Price Hill Improvement Association President Amber Kassem says she emailed police about the home on the 3700 block of Warsaw Avenue just hours before the shooting happened.“10:30 in the morning, sent an email. Can you give me an update on Warsaw? Activity still running up through there,” said Kassem as she showed WCPO 9 the email.WATCH: Why neighbors say they're concerned about the home, history of violationsWhen at the home on Wednesday, our crews saw that some of the windows were broken or had boards on them, and that there were people inside the house.“That property should have been boarded up. That block should be regularly patrolled,” said Kassem.Other community members also told us that this house has been a major concern in the neighborhood for quite some time. According to Hamilton County reports, the property has 23 violations dating back to 2007. Four are currently open for trash, litter and tall grass.There are also four open service requests for litter and bulk item pickup.The property is owned by an out-of-state company known as Second Avenue, according to the City of Cincinnati. Kassem said that’s part of the issue.“We have someone who doesn’t care about our community, who leaves it open because it's just part of their portfolio. And they don’t care about making sure it’s in good condition, or that it’s safe, or that it’s not a criminal platform for the entire city,” said Kassem.We reached out to the City of Cincinnati and police, asking if this property was on their radar and what they are doing to ensure the safety of the community. A city spokesperson replied with the following statement:“In August 2025, the City filed a lawsuit against Second Avenue, a large, national entity which owns over a hundred single-family rental properties in Cincinnati, including the structure located at 3752 Warsaw Avenue.On Friday, the City received a complaint this particular property was blighted. The City reached out to Second Avenue, who expressed their belief that the property was vacant. After communication from the City, Second Avenue indicated they would vacate the property and secure it as the property’s owner. The City did not have the authority to vacate and secure the premises. It does not appear as though Second Avenue made any attempt to secure the building.The City is taking steps today to ensure Second Avenue is meeting its obligations as a property owner in this community. The City continues to pursue its case against Second Avenue for substandard living conditions.”WCPO 9 News has attempted to reach the property owner but has so far been unsuccessful.

https://www.dw.com/en/swan-song-new-book.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5N0g7 Diana died in 1997, aged 36, in a car crash in Paris as she was being chased by paparazzi Image: John Stillwell/PA Wire/empics/picture alliance Advertisement Charles Spencer's book about his late sister Princess Diana's life and former marriage to Britain's now King Charles III hit bookstores on Tuesday. The book titled "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister" is being published globally by Penguin and has been translated into 12 languages. The memoir triggered a royal row even before it went on sale, after some of its pre-published extracts — laden with Spencer's explosive claims — received a rare reaction and rebuttal from the king. Charles Spencer, the 9th Earl Spencer, is Diana's younger brother and has long clashed with the royal House of Windsor over how they treated the princess. What does Charles Spencer say in his memoir of Princess Diana? In one of the claims that made a splash ahead the new book's release, Spencer accused Charles of sounding "giddily elated" and "like a lottery winner" when he had called him after Diana's death. Spencer also writes that he had argued against plans for Charles and Diana's sons, William and Harry , to walk in their mother's funeral procession in 1997, saying that she would not have wanted them to go through that ordeal. Spencer claims Charles "went ballistic" during the argument , telling him: "Rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough." William was 15-years-old at the time and Harry was 12. The world was moved by somber visuals of the young princes walking behind Diana's coffin. How has King Charles III reacted to Spencer's claims? Following the release of the book's excerpts last week, Buckingham Palace published a strongly-worded statement. "His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," it said in a statement considered rare as far as responses from the royal household go. Princess Diana's life and death In 1981, a 20-year-old Lady Diana Spencer married a 32-year-old Charles, who was then the Prince of Wales, in a fairytale wedding that was televised globally. Their whirlwind romance soon hit rock bottom and culminated in a public breakdown of their marriage. Diana famously told the BBC in an interview that "there were three of us in this marriage, so it was a bit crowded" in reference to Charles' ⁠relationship with Camilla Parker ​Bowles. Diana, known as the people's princess , was loved by people from all over the world. Her popularity led to her experiencing a media frenzy that lasted nearly all her adult life. The royal couple divorced in 1996 and Diana died a year later, aged 36, in a car crash in Paris as she was being pursued by paparazzi. Charles married Parker Bowles in 2005. https://metro.co.uk/2026/09/19/banker-st.text: Joanna Cierpka, 51 (pictured) denied murdering her partner Henrik Slotsaa after he told her he had met someone at work (Picture: Central News) A banker murdered by his partner offered her £70,000 and a plot of land in Greece in a split up deal, a court has heard. Henrik Slotsaa had admitted to his partner Joanna Cierpka on her birthday that he had met someone else he ‘liked’. Mr Slotsaa, 52, had offered Cierpka, 51, a financial settlement for a breakup, months before his body was found by police at their home in Elephant and Castle, south London. The Old Bailey was told officers found the Citibank worker dead in his bedroom in March, while Cierpka was discovered injured in the living room. Cierpka, from Poland, denied a charge of murder, but claims she is guilty of manslaughter by reason of her diminished responsibility. A prosecution psychiatrist has said jealousy over Mr Slotsaa’s new relationship with Aimee O’Shaughnessy could have played a part in his alleged murder. Mr Slotsaa had met Ms O’Shaughnessy at a work event last November, a couple of months after he started at Citibank’s Canary Wharf offices. The pair later exchanged numbers and had a lunch on at least a couple of occasions, including in January 2026, when Mr Slotsaa told Ms O”Shaughnessy he ‘enjoyed spending time’ with her, to which she replied she wasn’t ready to ‘get involved with someone’ at that point in her life. Asked what she understood their relationship status to be, Ms O’Shaughnessy told court they were just friends. Mr Slotsaa, 52, was found dead at his home in Elephant and Castle last March She added that Mr Slotsaa had mentioned having a ‘hard time’ in his current relationship with Cierpka, who he said was suffering from depression and had stopped taking her medication to treat it. Mr Slotsaa had confided in her plans to financially resolve things with Cierpka so they could separate, she told the court. She said: ‘He was very good with his numbers and he worked a plan out that he thought could potentially work. ‘But he was still very concerned about that because he didn’t think it was the right thing to do because his partner, he deemed her to be not coping.’ Asked what could have been on the table as part of an offer, Ms O’Shaughnessy said Mr Slotsaa was considering an offer of £70,000 and a plot of land in Greece. In one text message sent to Ms O’Shaughnessy, Mr Slotsaa wrote: ‘I always need you for some reason, I can’t explain.’ ‘We’re def friends for life so you are stuck with me’, she replied. Following her arrest, Cierpka told a psychiatrist that Mr Slotsaa had admitted last December that he no longer loved her and had met someone else at work. Jurors heard that she also told a member of staff at hospital that she had ‘killed her partner’, a remark which was recorded in a note dated and signed by her. The trial continues. https://www.dw.com/en/poland-arrests-man.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5O8DI Amid a spate of violence this week, Tusk said 'spontaneous' attacks were 'inspired by online activity' [FILE: October 8] Image: Albert Zawada/PAP/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Poland on Sunday detained a man accused of plotting to assassinate Prime Minister Donald Tusk and the country's defense minister, the PM wrote on X. "The man threatening an attack has been detained," Tusk wrote on X, praising the police for their "swift and decisive action." The Interior Minister also confirmed the arrest. No details about the man's identity were made public. Security chiefs convene urgent talks Tusk's tweet followed an emergency meeting by Poland's security services to discuss what officials said was a potential attack against both the prime minister and Defense ‌Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz. The meeting was convened at short notice after police received a tip-off about a possible assassination attempt, a spokesperson for the Interior Ministry wrote in a post on X. While the nature of the apparent threat was not immediately clear, Poland remains on high alert after a wave of violent attacks at schools in the country this week. Poland, which borders Ukraine, has also been facing growing security threats from hybrid attacks by Russia in recent months. What do we know about the school attacks in Poland? Poland is reeling from three knife attacks at schools in just four days this week, which have left at least one person dead and injured many others, including children. The first incident was on Wednesday, when a 19-year-old student at a vocational school in the central Mazovian province injured nine people when he attacked his fellow students and teachers with a sharp object. A day later, a 15-year-old killed a school caretaker and injured two others at his former school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, also in the same province. Tusk said the suspect had worn a camera mounted to his helmet to film the attack. On Saturday, a 21-year-old woman attacked an adult education school in Warsaw, wounding three other women. Polish police have detained 117 people across the country for carrying knives or dangerous weapons, as well as for threatening to attack schools or students. Police checked 64,000 schools, most of them in central Mazovian province. Police said Friday that cybercrime investigators have found no evidence that a social media challenge is fueling the wave of youth violence, or that the attacks were coordinated. What did Tusk say about the school attacks? On Sunday morning, Donald Tusk said the attacks were "spontaneous actions" that were fueled by rising "glorification of violence" online. "We are not dealing with any group organized on a big scale," Tusk said during the government crisis meeting. "In the past years and months, we have noted — globally and in Poland — a rise in the fascination with violence," Tusk continued. The prime minister blamed "nihilistic violence" for the wave of attacks, rather than a specific political ideology. However, he did acknowledge that "some of the people detained are active in the ultraright environment." Tusk added that authorities have observed an increase in online searches for Nazi or far-right content and for "mass killers who have become idols online." The prime minister pointed to a "civilizational phenomenon" of children becoming more exposed to violence online through video games or crime stories. Tusk added that police checks would continue at schools across the country next week to make sure children who have been exposed to these stories of knife attacks do not "get stupid and unsafe thoughts" of perpetrating copycat attacks. https://www.politico.eu/article/france-r.text: PARIS — Raphaël Glucksmann’s unexpectedly decisive victory in France’s center-left primary may have won him the backing and resources of the once-powerful Socialist Party, but the 46-year-old MEP needs even more support if he wants to drive his distinctly pro-European platform all the way to the Elysée Palace. All recent polls show Glucksmann is trailing far-right front-runner Marine Le Pen and her two main challengers for a spot in the presidential election’s second round: the far left’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon and center-right former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe. Mélenchon and Le Pen both want to fundamentally alter Paris’ relationship with Brussels, while Philippe is campaigning mostly on domestic issues. If he wants to win the presidency, Glucksmann, the leader of the moderate left party Place Publique, needs to woo several constituencies at once: the undecided left-leaning voters considering throwing their support behind Mélenchon’s surging campaign as well as the centrist voters already struggling to choose between Philippe and Gabriel Attal, the head of President Emmanuel Macron’s party. Advertisement Advertisement “We’re still a long way from the final list of candidates, and the political landscape is far from set in stone,” said Socialist MEP Christophe Clergeau, who had backed Glucksmann’s rival Olivier Faure in the center-left primary. “It’s up to [Glucksmann] to build momentum, unite the Socialist family … [and] reach out to all left-wing voters to demonstrate his ability to be our camp’s voice.” But Glucksmann and his allies are confident that his strong showing in the primary — he won more than 66% of the vote in the first round, more than four times as many votes as his nearest competitor — is a sign of good things to come. “All the citizens of the left who came, voted, took part have given me tremendous hope,” Glucksmann said in his victory speech. “The result is indisputable: I am tonight the candidate of the democratic left.” Aurore Lalucq, a fellow S&D MEP and co-president of Place Publique, said the result “isn’t far from a landslide.” “There is no doubt that his platform is widely supported, and that gives us the strength to rally others behind us,” she said. “The ability to unite comes from strength.” The next battle Glucksmann faces stiff competition from Mélenchon and his party, France Unbowed, for voters who lean left. Advertisement Advertisement Glucksmann has long refused to work with France Unbowed . He has accused Mélenchon of using antisemitic tropes — an allegation that the presidential candidate has denied — as well as being insufficiently supportive of Ukraine and too friendly with China. Jean-Luc Mélenchon waves after a campaign rally in Cournon-d’Auvergne in the Puy-de-Dôme department on October 11, 2026. | Adrien Fillon/ AFP via Getty Images Mélenchon has been courting support from the French Greens , whose candidate Marine Tondelier is struggling in the polls. Glucksmann is also eyeing support from the Greens, who have frequently teamed up with the Socialists in the past, including during the early years of François Hollande’s presidency. Tondelier is extremely critical of Glucksmann for his refusal to associate with France Unbowed and participate in a primary contest featuring the party. Her party, however, is increasingly torn between pro-Mélenchon and pro-Glucksmann voices. An individual close to Glucksmann, who was granted anonymity to discuss campaign strategy, said the MEP is looking to build new alliances and argued that the French Greens “are not limited to Marine Tondelier.” Then there’s the elephant inside the Socialist room. Hollande, the party’s last president who was elected in 2012 but chose not to run for reelection five years later due to dismal approval ratings, has dropped several clues about his plans to run for president again . He refused to take part in his party’s primary — instead waiting to see if the winner’s campaign would flail, giving him an opening to step in. Glucksmann said in an interview Monday that Hollande had called him to congratulate him on his win, but the former president has not made a public statement since the primary results. Advertisement Advertisement “I’ve known François Hollande for a long time … I’ll take him at his word, that he was waiting to see how things would look at the end of the year, and that if the momentum around the party’s primary candidate was strong, he wouldn’t undermine that momentum,” said Loïg Chesnais-Girard, the president of Brittany who backed Glucksmann in the primary. “The focus right now is on building that momentum. And then we’ll see how things play out,” Chesnais-Girard said.
